subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron runs get a first-class `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or remain limited to per-job `payload.toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: This defines a public config contract and scheduled-run security boundary across tool access, message delivery, and existing policy precedence, so automation should not choose it without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add cron-scoped policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` as the explicit scheduled-run policy layer and document/test how it composes with per-job `toolsAllow` and delivery requirements.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Make cron sessions participate in `tools.subagents.tools` only if maintainers want cron and subagents to share one operator-facing restriction model.

options.title: Keep per-job tools only
options.body: Decline a new config surface and instead document `payload.toolsAllow` as the cron restriction mechanism while adding targeted duplicate-delivery safeguards if needed.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` as the explicit scheduled-run policy layer and document/test how it composes with per-job `toolsAllow` and delivery requirements.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest available history across the current cron/tool/config surface and prior issue review context.
